data.text:
Super Typhoon #Uwan (international codename: Fung Wong), with a wingspan of 1800 kilometres practically covers the whole length of the Philippines from North to South in this imagery. It has been put on category 5. It is menacing and brings a lot of fear considering the history of many lives lost from previous natural disasters. 

Barely a few days since the island of Cebu was battered by Typhoon #Tino and still reeling from the aftermath of devastation it has left, Super typhoon #Uwan is so far the biggest and potentially the most severe to hit the country of over 116 million people. 

The Super Typhoon #Uwan has brought widespread panic in the entire country and its neighbours. Known to sit in the “ring of fire” for its many volcanic eruptions, the Philippines receives about 8-11 typhoons each year and is not foreign to natural disasters. Our people are normally very resilient and rise up each time. 
#GodblessthePhilippines

data.text:
Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 9 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Tropical Cyclone UWAN
Issued at: 5:00 AM, 10 November 2025(Monday)

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Tarlac, Bulacan(Hagonoy, Paombong, Malolos, Calumpit, Pulilan, Plaridel, Baliuag, Bustos, San Rafael, San Ildefonso, San Miguel, Guiguinto, Bulakan, Bocaue, Balagtas, Pandi, Angat, Santa Maria) and Nueva Ecija(Cabiao, San Antonio, San Isidro, Gapan).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is still THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Rizal, Metro Manila, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna, Nueva Ecija(General Tinio, Aliaga, Bongabon, Cabanatuan, Carranglan, Cuyapo, Gabaldon, General Mamerto Natividad, Guimba, Jaen, Laur, Licab, Llanera, Lupao, Nampicuan, Palayan, Pantabangan, Penaranda, Quezon, Rizal, San Jose, San Leonardo, Santa Rosa, Santo Domingo, Munoz, Talavera, Talugtug, Zaragoza), Bulacan(San Jose del Monte, Dona Remedios Trinidad, Marilao, Norzagaray, Obando, Meycauayan) and Quezon(General Nakar, Infanta, Real, Mauban, Sampaloc, Lucban, Sariaya, Candelaria, Dolores, Tiaong, San Antonio, Tayabas, Lucena, Pagbilao, Panukulan, Burdeos, Polillo).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate rains affecting Quezon(Agdangan, Alabat, Atimonan, Buenavista, Calauag, Catanauan, General Luna, Guinayangan, Gumaca, Jomalig, Lopez, Macalelon, Mulanay, Padre Burgos, Patnanungan, Perez, Pitogo, Plaridel, Quezon, San Andres, San Francisco, San Narciso, Tagkawayan, Unisan) which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 8:00 AM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
